title: Microcharge composer: per-invocation spend lens with CSV-first export
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact 'Microcharge Composer' UI that surfaces per-invocation and per-message spend at a developer-friendly granularity. The composer should prioritize CSV-first export for downstream accounting systems, include role-aware filters (owner, billing-admin, viewer), and surface a small inline rate-slab preview so finance teams can validate unit pricing before exporting. This ticket covers exploratory sketches, high-fidelity prototype, usability reviews, and a small spec for frontend engineering to implement the export API hooks.
acceptance_criteria: A compact composer panel exists in the Console mock that shows per-invocation rows with timestamp, route, model variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, applied_rate, and computed_charge
CSV export button produces a downloadable CSV matching the sample schema agreed with finance (header row + documented units), and includes role/route metadata
Role-aware filter presets (Owner / Billing / Viewer) toggle which columns and export fields are available, with clear disable states for restricted roles
Rate-slab preview shows current slab and next slab breakpoints for the selected period and updates when a different model variant or region is selected
Prototype usability test (5 sessions) yields no major blocking issues and a median SUS >= 70 for finding/exporting a per-invocation charge line
Design spec includes accessibility notes (keyboard focus order for composer rows, CSV export button accessible via aria-label), and a handoff-ready Figma file with export tokens and annotated spacing
design_notes: Motivation: Customers asked for a smaller, action-first pane to quickly inspect micro-level spend and ship reconciliations to accounting without navigating multiple downloads.
Focus on scanability: dense rows with optional expanded context for request payload preview (collapsed by default).
Privacy: hide payloads for viewer and billing roles by default; expose full prompt/message only for Owner and explicitly consented sessions.
Sampling tradeoff: we add a 'Sampled' badge for very high-volume routes and surface sampling ratio in CSV metadata. Full export falls back to job-based backend export (ENG work).
Export schema includes 'sampling_ratio' and 'exported_by' fields to make downstream reconciliation deterministic.
decisions: Use CSV-first strategy: customers often ingest CSVs into BI tools; adding JSON export postponed to follow-up to reduce scope.
Compact rows instead of heavy visual charts to optimize for quick reads and high-density listings on small consoles.
Rate-slab preview computed client-side from cached pricing tiles to avoid additional network roundtrips in the prototype. Backend will serve canonical slabs in ENG epic ENG-4412.
Role-aware column rendering will be implemented as an attribute map provided by the backend; design will supply allowed/forbidden states for each role to frontend.
Sampling: choose conservative default sampling (1%) for routes exceeding 100k invocations in the selected window to keep UI responsive.
feedback: PM Sofia Martinez: prefer CSV header names to follow finance conventions (unit_usd, tokens_in, tokens_out) — updated prototype to match.
Eng lead Noah Kim: flagged backend dependency for full export; suggested adding an explicit 'Request full export' CTA that triggers job ENG-4412.
Legal review (Samira Huang): remove any prompt text in viewer role exports; added sampling_ratio and redaction flag to schema.
UX review (internal): recommended increasing row contrast and adding a micro-heat indicator for high-charge rows — implemented in v2 frames.
Accessibility audit (contractor): keyboard focus order was inconsistent for expanded rows; fixed and annotated in Figma.
